HabiroCyclotomicCompletions.targets: Habiro's cyclotomic completion R[q]^S = lim_f R[q]/(f) over the multiplicative monoid of cyclotomic polynomials, with its topology and universal property; convergent factorial expansions in P_N(q)=prod(1-q^i) and coefficient algorithms; root evaluation and Taylor maps into R[zeta][[q-zeta]]; the connectedness/rigidity theorems (Habiro Thm 4.1, rootwise Taylor injectivity Thm 5.2, evaluation uniqueness Thm 6.1); completed modules, prime inversion and Chinese-remainder decomposition.
baselineHas: Mathlib Polynomial.cyclotomic and its irreducibility/divisibility API (Mathlib/RingTheory/Polynomial/Cyclotomic/*)
Mathlib AdicCompletion / IsAdicComplete and Ideal.Quotient inverse-limit machinery (Mathlib/RingTheory/AdicCompletion/Basic.lean)
Mathlib Polynomial.hasseDeriv (Mathlib/Algebra/Polynomial/HasseDeriv.lean), needed to identify the higher Taylor coefficients
Tau Ceti IsCyclotomicExtension/IsPrimitiveRoot API (TauCeti/NumberTheory/Cyclotomic/*) for the root-evaluation targets
missing: the directed system over cyclotomic-divisibility and its completion, with projections, density of polynomials, completeness/separatedness and the universal property (this is not the adic completion Mathlib has)
cofinality of the P_N system and the comparison with completion at q^m-1, with multiplicity counts
normalized factorial expansions, their uniqueness, and the finite-precision arithmetic/coefficient-extraction algorithms
evaluation at a root of order d and the Taylor map into R[zeta][[q-zeta]], naturality under conjugation, order restriction and q -> q^a, plus the p-adic re-expansion cocycle
adjacency of cyclotomic orders, the resultant/comaximality lemmas and the rigidity theorems 4.1/5.2/6.1
completed modules over the completion, exactness hypotheses/derived-limit correction, CRT splitting and the R = Z[1/p] examples
no external roadmap input: only the Mathlib polynomial-cyclotomic algebra marked UPSTREAM

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion.targets: Complete the elementary/algebraic entry layer: divisibility and multiplicative arithmetic (Mobius inversion, Dirichlet convolution); residues and reciprocity up to source-scoped higher reciprocity; sequences, Bernoulli/Euler numbers and generating functions; polynomial and matrix arithmetic (resultants, discriminants, Smith/Hermite/rational canonical forms); classical Diophantine equations; number-field arithmetic handoff; Mahler measure and Pisot/Salem classes; integral Galois modules, normal integral bases and locally free class groups.
baselineHas: Mathlib ArithmeticFunction.moebius and sum_eq_iff_sum_smul_moebius_eq (Mathlib/NumberTheory/ArithmeticFunction.lean)
Mathlib legendreSym.quadratic_reciprocity and gaussSum (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LegendreSymbol/*)
Mathlib bernoulli, Pell.* , Polynomial resultant/discriminant and Smith-normal-form API
Mathlib/NumberTheory/MahlerMeasure.lean plus Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory/* and class-group/unit-group API
missing: source-scoped higher reciprocity laws on top of the existing class field theory, and residue symbols at 2 and at infinite places
Christol-type bridges to algebraic power series in characteristic p, automatic sequences and radix families, which need their own statements
proved Mahler-measure lower bounds and certified Pisot/Salem classification, needing heights and canonical heights from DiophantineApproximation DT.0 and ArithmeticDynamics DY.1

integral Galois module theory: group-ring modules of rings of integers, normal-basis maps, locally free class groups, Noether tame NIB, Hilbert-Speiser and Froehlich, needing K0 of orders from KTheoryLowDegrees Z.1 (no K-theory of projectives in the baseline)
certified normal-form algorithms returning change-of-basis matrices and reconstruction equations
breadth is large but the stacking is shallow: most stages extend carriers the library already has

DirichletPadicLFunctions.targets: RJW Parts I in full: complex special values and algebraicity of L(chi,1-k) via generalized Bernoulli numbers and Gauss sums; the Dedekind zeta pole and residue; the smoothed measure F_a(T) and the Kubota-Leopoldt pseudo-measure zeta_p with its interpolation and Kummer congruences; interpolation for all Dirichlet characters via the tame-conductor measures zeta_eta; Teichmuller branches, log_p, Leopoldt's p-adic formula and the pole theorem; the Eisenstein coefficient measures and their weight specializations.

Mathlib riemannZeta_neg_nat_eq_bernoulli and HurwitzZetaValues (Mathlib/NumberTheory/LSeries/HurwitzZetaValues.lean)

pseudo-measures: the Amice inverse of F_a, psi-invariance, division by [a]-1 in the total quotient ring, independence of the smoothing parameter, and zeta_p with its interpolation and Kummer congruences
the twisted measures zeta_eta for tame conductor D>1 and the full RJW 5.1/5.7 interpolation, with descent and scalar extension
Teichmuller decomposition, a compatible p-adic logarithm with log_p(p)=0, Leopoldt's formula and the residue/pole theorem
the Eisenstein coefficient measures A_n and the measure-valued q-expansion specializing to p-stabilized E_k

supplier theory absent from the baseline: Tate zeta integrals (AutomorphicLFunctionsAndLocalFactors AL.1) for the Dedekind-zeta pole, and the unbounded Amice transform / character-and-weight spaces of LocallyAnalyticDistributions L1/L3
a separate p=2 branch on 1+4Z_2 with its corrected normalization

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/HopfRinow.targets: The Riemannian connection-and-geodesic layer culminating in Hopf-Rinow: the piecewise-C1 versus C1 length comparison and finiteness of riemannianEDist; existence, uniqueness and C-infinity regularity of the Levi-Civita connection; covariant differentiation along curves, geodesics, the geodesic spray and flow; the exponential map, normal neighbourhoods, the Gauss lemma and minimizing geodesics; the TFAE of geodesic completeness, properness, metric completeness and existence of minimizers; compactness corollaries and the metric length/geodesic-space API.

normal neighbourhoods and the local logarithm, normal coordinates
the Gauss lemma, ball-internal radial minimization with its equality case, and the escape estimate giving pathELength = edist on small radial segments
the first variation of energy and the criticality characterization of geodesics
the Hopf-Rinow TFAE itself: (c)=>(d) with convergence in TM, (d)=>(a_p), (a_p)=>(f_p) by minimizing on compact spheres, (a_p) and (f_p) => properness, and (b)<=>(e_p), plus base-point propagation
Layer 4 corollaries: compact implies geodesically complete, and transport of the whole theory across smooth Riemannian isometries

ArithmeticStatistics.targets: Prove source-qualified counting theorems for families ordered by height or discriminant: finiteness at bounded height and asymptotic densities with stabilizer weights; integral orbit parametrizations of number rings and genus-one models; lattice-point counting in fundamental domains with cusp and reducible-locus bounds and uniform tail estimates; field-counting and class-group distribution theorems; the Bhargava-Shankar average Selmer bound and its rank consequence; higher moments and function-field analogues.
baselineHas: Mathlib MeasureTheory/Group/GeometryOfNumbers.lean (Minkowski convex-body theorem) and NumberField CanonicalEmbedding/ConvexBody.lean

missing: arithmetic families with equivalence relations, height/discriminant orderings, local conditions and weighted counts, with finiteness at bounded height proved before any density

integral invariant theory and orbit-to-object bijections for number rings and genus-one models, including nonmaximal, reducible and degenerate loci (no binary cubic/quartic form parametrization in the baseline)
counting lattice points in fundamental domains, cusp and reducible-contribution bounds, and uniform tail theorems allowing infinitely many local conditions
the actual counting and class-group moment theorems by discriminant and signature
a complete Bhargava-Shankar Selmer orbit count and the resulting rank inequality

supplier theory absent from the baseline: successive-minima/convex-body refinements (GeometryOfNumbers GN.1), the large sieve and bilinear sums (SieveMethods SV.2), weak Mordell-Weil and descent exact sequences (Heights RP.1), curves/divisors/Picard objects (SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.3), and normal-form arithmetic (ClassicalArithmeticCompletion CA.3)

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ZigzagPreprojecti.targets: Zigzag algebras of finite simple graphs and their skew variants with bases, centers and symmetric Frobenius traces; graded Cartan matrices C_G(q)=(1+q^2)I+qA_G; preprojective algebras with orientation independence; the quadratic dual and the theorem that path-graded zigzag is Koszul exactly off finite ADE; the 2-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebra and its identification with the 2-Calabi-Yau completion; derived Koszul duality, the Hochschild comparison HH^{2,q} and Liu-Wang's intrinsic-formality classification for trees; braid-group actions by two-term bimodule complexes and their comparison with Seidel-Thomas spherical twists.

Tau Ceti TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Preprojective/{Basic,Grading,Orientation,Gauge,Opposite}.lean
Tau Ceti TauCeti/LinearAlgebra/RootSystem/AffineDynkinType/* (affine simply-laced diagrams, deletion, positive semidefiniteness, star descriptions) and Quiver/PathAlgebra/*, Quiver/Symmetrify.lean
Tau Ceti TauCeti/Algebra/Homology/{DG/Algebra/*, AInfinity/{Algebra,Stasheff,Coderivation}} and Mathlib DerivedCategory/HomotopyCategory/Triangulated
missing: Koszul duality for graded algebras: Koszul complexes, exactness, Hilbert-series identities, handedness of left and right quadratic duals, and the Koszulity criterion (no Koszul-duality API anywhere in the baseline)
the signless quadratic dual and its rescaling comparison with the signed preprojective relation, including the non-bipartite sign obstruction

2-dimensional Ginzburg DG algebras, H^0 identification with the preprojective algebra, and Calabi-Yau completions under Keller's hypotheses (no CalabiYau in the baseline), plus the 3-dimensional quiver-with-potential version
Hochschild cohomology of a DG/graded algebra with its small cofibrant bimodule resolution and the bigraded HH^{2,q} comparison (no Hochschild theory in the baseline)
derived Koszul duality RHom over the Ginzburg algebra, minimal A-infinity deformations and the intrinsic-formality criterion, then Liu-Wang's exact characteristic-dependent theorem
braid bimodule complexes, their inverse/commuting/braid homotopy equivalences, and Seidel-Thomas spherical twists with Serre duality (neither spherical objects nor Serre duality are in the baseline)

GlobalGaloisDeformations.targets: Global Galois deformation problems over number fields: framed and unframed deformation functors over Artinian coefficient rings, representability and universal representations, local conditions and the global-to-local presentation with its exact variable and relation counts (KW II Prop 4.5/Cor 4.7), restriction/twisting/change of problem, Taylor-Wiles auxiliary primes with prescribed Frobenius eigenvalues and dual-Selmer reduction, and the polarized dimension-n and determinant-variable problems of ACC+ 6.2 with g = qn - n^2[F+:Q].

Mathlib IsAdicComplete / AdicCompletion/LocalRing.lean for complete local coefficient rings

continuous and derived Galois cohomology with Poitou-Tate duality, Selmer and dual-Selmer comparisons (ArithmeticGaloisDuality R02.1/R02.2/R02.6/D7/D8)
complete local coefficient categories, Schlessinger/Mazur representability and obstruction algebra (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1/R03.2); no deformation functor exists in the baseline
local deformation rings, including the local models of LocalGaloisDeformationRings L7/L8 which themselves consume the p-adic Hodge period functors R06.2

the roadmap's own eight stages: deformation functors, representability, global presentations and relation bounds, restriction/twisting with p=2 branches, the Taylor-Wiles prime construction, and the polarized/determinant-variable ACC+ problems

tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/OptimalTransport.targets: The whole transport chain: couplings, gluing and kernels; existence and stability of optimal plans; general Kantorovich duality with c-transforms and optimality certificates; Wasserstein spaces and their topology; the Monge problem; the convex-analysis tower with Brenier and polar factorization; Monge-Ampere measures and regularity (Aleksandrov, Caffarelli, Ma-Trudinger-Wang); Riemannian Brenier-McCann; dynamic plans and Benamou-Brenier; displacement convexity; abstract metric gradient flows; entropy, JKO and PDE flows; barycenters; entropic transport, Sinkhorn and Schrodinger bridges; CD/RCD synthetic curvature; Gromov-Wasserstein.

Mathlib ProbabilityTheory.Kernel with disintegration, and MeasureTheory.Measure.map/prod
Mathlib convexity API: ConvexOn.locallyLipschitzOn_interior, intrinsicInterior, affineSpan, and eVariationOn (Mathlib/Analysis/BoundedVariation.lean)

Monge-Ampere theory: Aleksandrov measures, comparison and maximum principles, Alexandrov twice-differentiability, viscosity/Aleksandrov/Sobolev bridges, Caffarelli regularity and MTW partial regularity

Riemannian Brenier-McCann, which needs the rest of the HopfRinow roadmap (exponential map, minimizing geodesics, Hopf-Rinow) plus injectivity radius, squared-distance semiconcavity, cut-locus measurability and Riemannian volume and curvature from GeometricTopology Layer 7

measured kernels and Gromov-Wasserstein, plus the public API layer

HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves.targets: The Hilbert examples of Shimura theory for every totally real F: the two data and their domains; abelian schemes with real multiplication, c-polarization modules and Hilbert-Blumenthal moduli; Deligne-Pappas integral models at arbitrary and ramified p with the Rapoport locus, ordinary locus and Hasse ideal; the arithmetic quotient and unit action with Delta(N); p-level structures and effective groups; twisted torsion moduli with prescribed local behaviour; quaternionic Shimura curves, their compactifications and integral models (Carayol); definite quaternionic algebraic forms and Taylor-Wiles freeness; cohomology and Hecke correspondences; Cerednik-Drinfeld bad-prime uniformisation.

Weil I and the needed Weil II results for the Hecke/cohomology stage (WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.5), on top of an etale cohomology theory the baseline does not have at all

its own thirteen stages, including Deligne-Pappas models at ramified p and p=2, the Hasse ideal and formal blow-up models, the twisted torsion moduli with prescribed real and local loci, Carayol's bad reduction of Shimura curves, and the Drinfeld upper half-plane with Cerednik-Drinfeld uniformisation

cycle complexes, motivic cohomology and cycle-class functoriality (MotivicEtaleKTheory M.4), and continuous derived Galois cohomology with dimension-general duality (ArithmeticGaloisDuality D7)

p-adic Hodge regulator theory: Bloch-Kato exponentials, the big logarithm and explicit interpolation (PadicHodgeRegulators L1/L3), which sits on the full PadicHodgeTheory period-ring/period-functor stack and on the (phi,Gamma)-module and Wach-module theory of PhiGammaModulesAndIwasawaCohomology

Iwasawa cohomology and control theorems (SelmerIwasawaCohomology L3), ordinary projectors and integral Hida families (PadicFamilies L0a/L1), generic Euler/Kolyvagin system machinery (EulerSystemsAndKolyvaginSystems ES.3/ES.4), and Hsieh's anticyclotomic mu-invariant theorem (AutomorphicPadicLFunctions L3h)

its own nine stages: the projectors with their integrality, the cycles and both Abel-Jacobi realizations, the corrected local conditions of CH section 7, universal norms, the CH Theorem 4.9 and 5.7 formulas, the Kolyvagin system with hypotheses (H.1)-(H.5), the Castella two-variable reciprocity and Yager-module comparison, and the weight-two identification

judgements.reason: Habiro must build its whole tower from nothing: the directed system over cyclotomic divisibility and its completion, P_N cofinality, normalized factorial expansions, Taylor maps into R[zeta][[q-zeta]] and the rigidity theorems 4.1/5.2/6.1, five layers deep. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion is far broader but mostly extends carriers Mathlib already has (moebius inversion, quadratic reciprocity, bernoulli, Pell, resultants, MahlerMeasure.lean); its only deep gaps are integral Galois modules needing K0 of orders and proved Mahler/Pisot-Salem bounds needing heights.

DirichletPadicLFunctions stacks five new layers - generalized Bernoulli and Gauss-sum L-values, the smoothed measure and the Kubota-Leopoldt pseudo-measure, twisted interpolation for all characters, Teichmuller branches with Leopoldt's formula, and Eisenstein coefficient measures - and additionally needs Tate zeta integrals and the unbounded Amice/character-space theory, none of which is in the baseline. ClassicalArithmeticCompletion sits almost entirely on existing Mathlib arithmetic (moebius, reciprocity, bernoulli, Pell, Smith normal form).

HopfRinow has roughly two and a half layers left - the exponential map, normal balls with the Gauss lemma and minimizing geodesics, and the TFAE itself - on top of a Levi-Civita connection with regularity, geodesic spray and maximal-interval extension that are already in Mathlib and Tau Ceti, and it needs no other roadmap. DirichletPadicLFunctions needs pseudo-measures, zeta_p, twisted interpolation and p-adic logarithms built from scratch plus Tate zeta integrals and locally analytic distributions from two further roadmaps.

ArithmeticStatistics has nothing in the baseline for its core objects - no integral orbit parametrization of number rings or genus-one models, no fundamental-domain lattice counting with cusp cutoffs, no uniform tail estimates - and six strictly stacked stages plus supplier theory (large sieve and bilinear sums, weak Mordell-Weil descent, Picard objects). HopfRinow needs only the exponential map, Gauss lemma and minimizing geodesics, and the TFAE, over an already-built connection-and-spray layer.

Zigzag's first five layers are already in Tau Ceti (about thirty Zigzag files plus Preprojective and AffineDynkinType), leaving four layers: Koszul duality, Ginzburg DG algebras with Calabi-Yau completion, Hochschild cohomology with A-infinity formality, and spherical twists. ArithmeticStatistics has zero baseline coverage of Bhargava-style orbit parametrization, cusp-bounded counting in fundamental domains and uniform tails, and its six stages sit on five further supplier stages that are equally absent.

GlobalGaloisDeformations has no starting point in the baseline: continuous Galois representations, Poitou-Tate duality and derived Galois cohomology, Schlessinger representability over complete local coefficient categories and local deformation rings are all absent, and its dimension-n stages additionally consume the p-adic Hodge period functors, above which its own eight stages sit. Zigzag has Layers 0-4 already built in Tau Ceti and needs four further layers of homological algebra.

OptimalTransport's remaining eleven layers are individually huge (Caffarelli and MTW regularity, metric gradient flows, RCD curvature, Schrodinger bridges) but its first five layers already exist in Tau Ceti and everything else rests on Mathlib measure theory, kernels and convexity. GlobalGaloisDeformations starts from nothing at all - no continuous Galois representation, no deformation functor, no Poitou-Tate duality, no local deformation ring - and must stack four supplier roadmaps, one of which reaches into the p-adic Hodge period functors, under its own eight stages.

HilbertModularVarieties consumes the entire Shimura programme (ShimuraData and ShimuraVarieties V8 with Baily-Borel, Borel algebraicity and canonical models), PEL moduli and abelian schemes, and Weil II on top of an etale cohomology theory the baseline lacks completely, before its own thirteen stages including Deligne-Pappas models at ramified p and Cerednik-Drinfeld uniformisation. OptimalTransport, though large, has five layers built and its missing layers sit directly on Mathlib measure theory and convexity.

Both start near zero, but HilbertModularVarieties needs the whole Shimura canonical-model theory, PEL and abelian-scheme moduli, compactifications, automorphic bundles, local smooth representation theory and Weil II before its own thirteen stages, whereas PhiGamma needs the Robba and period rings, then eight stages of (phi,Gamma)-module theory (Fontaine equivalence, overconvergence, Herr, psi, Wach, KPX) resting on a substantial Huber/adic-space and Witt-vector base already in Tau Ceti and Mathlib.

ArithmeticKTheory cannot even state its targets until higher algebraic K-theory exists: the baseline has no Q-construction, no K_1, K_2 or Milnor K-theory, no motivic or etale K-theory, and it further needs Quillen's finite-field computation, Borel's stable cohomology theorem for the ranks and a cyclotomic index formula. PhiGamma needs the period and Robba rings plus eight technical layers, but Witt vectors, perfection, fontaineTheta and a large Huber/adic-space base already exist.

Both need an absent foundation, but PadicHodgeTheory's is larger: beyond B_cris, B_st and the period functors it consumes perfectoid spaces with almost purity, A_inf cohomology, crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology, the pro-etale site and the actual comparison theorems, nearby cycles and Weil II, and the whole eight-layer (phi,Gamma)-module roadmap - and the baseline has no etale or crystalline cohomology at all. ArithmeticKTheory must build higher K-theory, Borel's theorem and etale K-theory, but its cohomological needs stay largely Galois-cohomological over number rings.

ShimuraVarieties needs complex analytic spaces and GAGA, reduction theory, Baily-Borel, Borel algebraicity, complex multiplication and Milne's conjugation theorem, none of which exist in the baseline, plus PEL and abelian-scheme moduli - a deep stack. PadicHodgeTheory's is deeper still: fourteen supplier roadmaps including perfectoid spaces, A_inf, crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology, the pro-etale site, the C_cris/C_dR/C_st comparison theorems, Weil II and the entire (phi,Gamma)-module roadmap, with only fontaineTheta and B_dR^+ present today.

GeneralizedHeegnerCycles consumes the CM and canonical-model side of ShimuraVarieties itself (through HeegnerPointEulerSystems HE.0-HE.1) and then adds motivic cycle complexes, Bloch-Kato and big-logarithm regulators resting on the full p-adic Hodge and (phi,Gamma)-module stack, Iwasawa cohomology, Hida families, Euler and Kolyvagin systems and Hsieh's nonvanishing theorem, before its own nine stages. ShimuraVarieties, though deep, stops at the canonical models.

GlobalGaloisDeformations needs continuous Galois representations, Poitou-Tate duality, Schlessinger representability and local deformation rings, then eight stages of deformation algebra. GeneralizedHeegnerCycles needs all of the CM and modular-curve geometry, motivic cycle complexes and Abel-Jacobi maps, p-adic Hodge regulators with the big logarithm, Iwasawa cohomology, Hida families and Kolyvagin systems, each an absent roadmap in its own right, before its nine stages of cycle geometry and explicit reciprocity.

HopfRinow's connection, regularity, spray, maximal-interval and inverse-function-theorem layers are already in Mathlib and Tau Ceti, leaving the exponential map, normal balls with the Gauss lemma and minimizers, the TFAE and its corollaries. Habiro must build all six of its layers - the cyclotomic directed system and its completion, P_N cofinality, factorial expansions, Taylor maps, the adjacency and rigidity theorems, and completed modules - with only Polynomial.cyclotomic and generic adic-completion machinery to start from.

ArithmeticStatistics needs orbit parametrizations, fundamental-domain counting with cusp cutoffs and uniform tails over a Minkowski/class-number base that does exist, six stages plus five supplier stages. ShimuraVarieties needs an entirely absent stack - hermitian symmetric domains, reduction theory and Siegel sets, complex analytic spaces with GAGA and Chow, Baily-Borel, resolution-based compactification for Borel's theorem, CM theory and Milne's conjugation argument - under its own ten stages.

Both sit at the top. HilbertModularVarieties needs the full Shimura canonical-model theory including Milne's conjugation step, PEL and abelian-scheme moduli, compactifications and Weil II, then Carayol and Cerednik-Drinfeld. GeneralizedHeegnerCycles needs the CM and modular-curve geometry too, but adds the whole p-adic and Iwasawa side on top of it: motivic cycle complexes, Bloch-Kato and big-logarithm regulators over the p-adic Hodge and (phi,Gamma)-module stack, Iwasawa cohomology, Hida families, Kolyvagin systems and Hsieh's theorem.

Zigzag has Layers 0-4 in the library and needs four further layers - Koszul duality, Ginzburg DG algebras with Calabi-Yau completion, Hochschild cohomology with A-infinity formality, and braid/spherical twists - over an existing DG and A-infinity base. PadicHodgeTheory needs B_cris, B_st, the period functors, perfectoid spaces, A_inf, crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology, the pro-etale site, the comparison theorems and Weil II, with essentially nothing beyond fontaineTheta and B_dR^+ in place.

OptimalTransport's eleven remaining layers are very large, but they rest on Mathlib measure theory, kernels, convexity and metric geometry, and five layers are already built in Tau Ceti. ArithmeticKTheory cannot state K_n(O_{F,S}) at all until higher algebraic K-theory is built: no Q-construction, K_1, K_2, Milnor or etale K-theory exists, and it then needs Quillen's finite-field computation, Borel's stable cohomology theorem and motivic-etale comparisons before any of its twelve stages.

Mathlib gives DirichletPadicLFunctions a strong start (Dirichlet L-functions with continuation and functional equation, zeta at negative integers via Bernoulli, the Mahler basis and the Amice transform), but it still needs generalized Bernoulli theory, pseudo-measures and zeta_p, twisted interpolation, p-adic logarithms and Eisenstein measures, plus Tate zeta integrals and locally analytic distributions from two absent roadmaps. Habiro's six layers are all new but self-contained commutative algebra over Polynomial.cyclotomic with no external supplier.

The two share suppliers - both need continuous Galois representations with duality and both reach into the p-adic Hodge period rings (PhiGamma through the annulus foundations, GlobalGaloisDeformations through the local models of L7/L8). PhiGamma's own content is the larger body: Robba and field-of-norms coefficient rings, Fontaine's equivalence in both directions, Cherbonnier-Colmez overconvergence, Herr complexes with Tate duality, the psi operator, the Iwasawa comparison, Wach modules and the KPX relative theory, against eight stages of deformation algebra for which Tau Ceti already supplies Chebotarev with auxiliary primes.

ClassicalArithmeticCompletion is broad but shallow: moebius inversion, quadratic reciprocity, Gauss sums, bernoulli, Pell, resultants, Smith normal form and MahlerMeasure.lean are all in Mathlib, leaving higher reciprocity, proved Mahler/Pisot bounds and integral Galois modules. Zigzag must build four layers of homological machinery that is wholly absent - Koszul duality with its complexes and Hilbert-series identities, Ginzburg DG algebras and Calabi-Yau completions, Hochschild cohomology with A-infinity deformation theory, and spherical twists with Serre duality.

ArithmeticStatistics needs orbit parametrizations, cusp-bounded counting and uniform tails plus a handful of supplier stages, all of it classical analysis and geometry of numbers over a base that already has Minkowski, class numbers and units. PadicHodgeTheory needs perfectoid spaces, A_inf, crystalline and derived de Rham cohomology, etale cohomology of schemes and of adic spaces, the pro-etale site, Weil II, the p-adic monodromy theorem and the (phi,Gamma)-module roadmap before B_cris, the period functors and the comparison theorems can even be stated.

OptimalTransport's remaining eleven layers are enormous in volume, but five layers exist in Tau Ceti and the rest builds on Mathlib measure theory, kernels, convexity and metric geometry. ShimuraVarieties has no starting point: hermitian symmetric domains, reduction theory and Siegel sets, complex analytic spaces with GAGA and Chow, complex multiplication and resolution-based compactification are all absent, and Baily-Borel, Borel algebraicity and Milne's conjugation theorem stack on top of them.
